review_note: At duality.tex line 5638 the source states δ_X(x)-δ_S(f(x))=trdeg_{κ(f(x))}κ(x) when X/S finite type and ω_X normalized relative to ω_S; the draft preserves both normalized dimension functions, the fibre-point quantifier and the residue-field transcendence degree.
statement:
Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. The normalized object includes the local identifications, not merely the derived isomorphism class of $D_T$. For a dualizing complex $D_T$ on a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, its associated dimension function $\delta_T:T\to\mathbf Z$ assigns to $t$ the unique integer such that the stalk $D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)]$ is a *normalized* dualizing complex over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, i.e. $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T,t}}(\kappa(t),D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)])\simeq\kappa(t)[0]$. For $x\in X$ above $y\in Y$, let $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ be the fibre and $\dim_x(X_y)$ its local topological dimension at $x$ (minimum dimension of neighbourhoods in the fibre). Let $f:X\to S$ be of finite type, and $D_X$ normalized relative to $D_S$. For every $x\in X$, with $s=f(x)$, one has
\[
\delta_X(x)-\delta_S(s)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x).
\]
Here $\delta_X,\delta_S$ are normalized dualizing dimension functions, and $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is the induced residue-field extension.
hypotheses: Finite type X/S, dualizing D_X normalized relative D_S, dimension function by normalized stalk.
conclusions: Difference of dimension functions equals transcendence degree of residue field.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-good-dualizing-dimension-function}
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme and let $\omega_S^\bullet$ be a
dualizing complex. Let $f : X \to S$ be of finite type
and let $\omega_X^\bullet$ be the dualizing complex
normalized relative to $\omega_S^\bullet$. For all $x \in X$ we have
$$
\delta_X(x) - \delta_S(f(x)) = \text{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}(\kappa(x))
$$
where $\delta_S$, resp.\ $\delta_X$
is the dimension function of
$\omega_S^\bullet$, resp.\ $\omega_X^\bullet$, see
Lemma \ref{lemma-dimension-function-scheme}.

statement:
Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. For a dualizing complex $D_T$ on a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, its associated dimension function $\delta_T:T\to\mathbf Z$ assigns to $t$ the unique integer such that the stalk $D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)]$ is a *normalized* dualizing complex over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, i.e. $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T,t}}(\kappa(t),D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)])\simeq\kappa(t)[0]$. For $x\in X$ above $y\in Y$, let $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ be the fibre and $\dim_x(X_y)$ its local topological dimension at $x$ (minimum dimension of neighbourhoods in the fibre). Let $x\in X$, $y=f(x)$. If $H^i(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x$ is nonzero, then
\[
i\ge-\dim_x(X_y).
\]
This is a lower bound for degrees of the upper-shriek structure complex; without extra hypotheses there is no asserted universal upper bound.
hypotheses: f in FTS_S, x∈X, y=f(x), fibre dimension at x defined.
conclusions: Nonzero cohomology of f^!O_Y can occur only in degrees at least minus the fibre dimension.

\label{lemma-shriek}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. Let $x \in X$ with image $y \in Y$. Then
$$
H^i(f^!\mathcal{O}_Y)_x \not = 0
\Rightarrow - \dim_x(X_y) \leq i.
$$

statement:
Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. For a dualizing complex $D_T$ on a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, its associated dimension function $\delta_T:T\to\mathbf Z$ assigns to $t$ the unique integer such that the stalk $D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)]$ is a *normalized* dualizing complex over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, i.e. $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T,t}}(\kappa(t),D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)])\simeq\kappa(t)[0]$. For $x\in X$ above $y\in Y$, let $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ be the fibre and $\dim_x(X_y)$ its local topological dimension at $x$ (minimum dimension of neighbourhoods in the fibre). Assume $f$ is flat. If $H^i(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x\ne0$, then
\[
-\dim_x(X_y)\le i\le0.
\]
If *every* geometric fibre of $f$ has dimension at most a fixed $d\ge0$, then $f^!\mathcal O_Y$, regarded as a complex of $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-modules, has Tor-amplitude in $[-d,0]$ (its derived tensor with any degree-zero $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-module has cohomology only in that range).
hypotheses: f flat in FTS_S, fibre dimension at x; a uniform bound d for the relative Tor statement.
conclusions: Cohomology lies between negative fibre dimension and zero, with relative Tor amplitude bounded by global fibre dimension.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-shriek}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. Let $x \in X$ with image $y \in Y$.
If $f$ is flat, then
$$
H^i(f^!\mathcal{O}_Y)_x \not = 0
\Rightarrow - \dim_x(X_y) \leq i \leq 0.
$$
In fact, if all fibres of $f$ have dimension $\leq d$, then
$f^!\mathcal{O}_Y$ has tor-amplitude in $[-d, 0]$ as an object
of $D(X, f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_Y)$.

review_note: At line 5717 the source requires O_{Y,y} Cohen–Macaulay and trdeg of GENERIC POINTS of each component through x ≤r. It concludes i≥-r for nonzero f^!O_Y stalk cohomology and Serre S2 for H^{-r}. The draft preserves both hypotheses and both conclusions.
statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. Let $x\in X$, $y=f(x)$, and assume the Noetherian local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is Cohen–Macaulay (its depth equals its Krull dimension). Suppose for every generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of $X$ containing $x$, the residue extension satisfies $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(\xi))}\kappa(\xi)\le r$ for some integer $r\ge0$. Then $H^i(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x\ne0$ implies $i\ge-r$. Moreover the finitely generated $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $H^{-r}(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x$ satisfies Serre's condition $(S_2)$: for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, its localization has depth at least $\min\{2,\dim\operatorname{Supp}(H^{-r}(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x)_{\mathfrak p}\}$, with the usual convention for zero modules.
hypotheses: Y local ring CM at y, generic component trdeg≤r for all components through x.
conclusions: Lower bound -r on cohomology and Serre S2 property of H^{-r} stalk.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-shriek-over-CM}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. Let $x \in X$ with image $y \in Y$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$ is Cohen-Macaulay, and
\item $\text{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(\xi))}(\kappa(\xi)) \leq r$
for any generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component
of $X$ containing $x$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
$$
H^i(f^!\mathcal{O}_Y)_x \not = 0
\Rightarrow - r \leq i
$$
and the stalk $H^{-r}(f^!\mathcal{O}_Y)_x$ is $(S_2)$ as an
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module.

statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. If $f:X\to Y$ is flat and quasi-finite, then the complex $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ has cohomology only in degree zero, so there exists a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\omega_{X/Y}=H^0(f^!\mathcal O_Y)$ with $f^!\mathcal O_Y\simeq\omega_{X/Y}[0]$. The sheaf $\omega_{X/Y}$ is flat over $Y$ via the morphism $f$.
conclusions: Upper shriek structure complex is a degree-zero coherent module flat over the target.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-quasi-finite-shriek}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. If $f$ is flat and quasi-finite, then
$$
f^!\mathcal{O}_Y = \omega_{X/Y}[0]
$$
for some coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\omega_{X/Y}$ flat over $Y$.

statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. Suppose $f$ is a Cohen–Macaulay morphism: flat and locally of finite presentation with Cohen–Macaulay scheme-theoretic fibres. Let $d:X\to\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ denote its locally constant relative fibre dimension. Then there is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\omega_{X/Y}$, flat over $Y$, for which $f^!\mathcal O_Y\simeq\omega_{X/Y}[d]$ locally on each component where $d$ is constant. Equivalently, the only nonzero cohomology sheaf occurs in cohomological degree $-d$ and is $\omega_{X/Y}$. The relative shift is componentwise when the relative dimension varies.
hypotheses: f CM in FTS_S, locally constant relative dimension d.
conclusions: f^!O_Y is a single coherent target-flat module shifted by the relative dimension.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-CM-shriek}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. If $f$ is Cohen-Macaulay (More on Morphisms, Definition
\ref{more-morphisms-definition-CM}), then
$$
f^!\mathcal{O}_Y = \omega_{X/Y}[d]
$$
for some coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\omega_{X/Y}$ flat over $Y$
where $d$ is the locally constant
function on $X$ which gives the relative dimension of $X$ over $Y$.
